extracted.intended_audience: factory managers, industrialists, foremen, employment/manufacturing supervisors
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidelines and standards for organizing, staffing, safeguarding, and improving factory production and labour practices; covers hiring, promotion, suggestion systems, job classification, safety, and shop environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit business titles / avoid title-based division of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Titles in business have been greatly overdone... The very necessity for the advice showed a condition that needed more than advice to correct it. And the correction is just this--abolish the titles."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dividing responsibility according to titles because it fragments and removes responsibility ('passing the buck'). Keep only a few legally necessary or publicly useful titles; otherwise 'get rid of them.' Titles should not be used as a substitute for real work or responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hire people for present ability and desire to work, not past history
rubrics_metrics.description: "We do not hire experts--neither do we hire men on past experiences... we do not care in the least about a man's antecedents--we do not hire a man's history, we hire the man."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not refuse applicants because of past mistakes, criminal record, or schooling; applicants start at the lowest position and must prove ability. The primary hiring criterion is the worker's desire to work and capacity to perform, not prior credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote by demonstrated work and ability, not by fixed positions or titles
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have so few titles that a man who ought to be doing something better... very soon gets to doing it--he is not restrained by the fact that there is no position ahead of him 'open'--for there are no 'positions.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid cut-and-dried places; let 'the best men make their places.' Promotion is informal: a man simply finds himself doing something else and getting more pay. Advancement requires both industry and leadership ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate departments by rate of production (output per worker)
rubrics_metrics.description: "A department gets its standing on its rate of production. The rate of production... is gained by dividing the number of parts produced by the number of hands working."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foremen should track daily production figures; superintendents tabulate scores and investigate low output. This simple rule-of-thumb measurement provides incentive for better methods and reduces personal bias in selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foremen should focus on production, not on cost accounting or personal favoritism
rubrics_metrics.description: "The foreman need not be a cost accountant... His charges are the machines and the human beings in his department. When they are working at their best he has performed his service."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep foremen concentrating on improving output and methods. Using production-rate metrics discourages selecting people based on personal preference and exposes favoritism through departmental records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain an open suggestion system and adopt worker ideas that yield verifiable savings
rubrics_metrics.description: "The whole factory management is always open to suggestion, and we have an informal suggestion system by which any workman can communicate any idea that comes to him and get action on it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify savings precisely (to the thousandth of a cent); adopt changes that pay for themselves within a reasonable time (example threshold: ~three months). Examples include conveyors, fixtures reducing manual burr removal, material substitutions, and processing changes that greatly reduce scrap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculate savings rigorously and use payback thresholds for change adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: "The saving of a cent per piece may be distinctly worth while... the calculations are carried out to the thousandth part of a cent. If the new way suggested shows a saving and the cost of making the change will pay for itself within a reasonable time--say within three months--the change is made practically as of course."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposed process changes by precise cost-benefit analysis and a clear payback period. Consider both production-increasing and labor-easing improvements; many changes that ease work also reduce cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize, measure, and make processes foolproof to reduce need for individual skill
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is the pressing to take away the necessity for skill in any job done by any one... The heat treatment in the hardening of steel is highly important... We introduced a system by which the man at the furnace has nothing at all to do with the heat... Coloured electric lights give him his signals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace hit-or-miss, rule-of-thumb operations with measured controls and signals so less-skilled operators can get consistent results. Use instruments (pyrometers, indicators) and automation where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prototype and test machine designs thoroughly before implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: "None of our machines is ever built haphazardly. The idea is investigated in detail before a move is made. Sometimes wooden models are constructed or again the parts are drawn to full size on a blackboard... we leave nothing to luck."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate ideas in detail, build models or full-size drawings, and iterate until the machine reliably performs the designed work. Most experiments should be tested; Ford cites about 90% success in experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage industrial creativity and apply creative thinking to industrial and social design
rubrics_metrics.description: "We want artists in industrial relationship. We want masters in industrial method... We want those who can mould the political, social, industrial, and moral mass into a sound and shapely whole."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value creative problem-solvers who design practical systems that improve workers' welfare and productivity. Creative effort should be directed to 'well-thought-out working designs' that are practicable and profitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept that most jobs are repetitive; classify jobs (A/B/C) and allow workers to progress as they prefer
rubrics_metrics.description: "The work in each department is classified according to its desirability and skill into Classes 'A,' 'B,' and 'C'... A man comes directly from the employment office to 'Class C.' As he gets better he goes into 'Class B,' and so on into 'Class A.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that many workers prefer steady, less-responsible jobs. Provide a clear classification and advancement path for those who choose to progress; allow workers agency in choosing to stay in production or move to toolmaking/supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze and classify every job by detailed physical and environmental requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: "To discover just what was the real situation, I had all of the different jobs in the factory classified to the kind of machine and work--whether the physical labour involved was light, medium, or heavy; whether it were a wet or a dry job... whether it required accuracy; whether the light was natural or artificial; ... the number of pieces that had to be handled per hour; the weight of the material handled; and the description of the strain upon the worker."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform comprehensive job analysis to identify which roles can be filled by people with various physical limitations. Use the analysis to match employees to appropriate tasks and to discover opportunities for subdivision and accommodation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide work opportunities to the physically incapacitated by subdividing tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: "If work is sufficiently subdivided... there will be no dearth of places in which the physically incapacitated can do a man's job and get a man's wage... out of 7,882 kinds of jobs, 4,034... did not require full physical capacity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not relegate disabled people to unremunerative hand labour; instead, identify and allocate factory tasks that match their capabilities so they can earn full wages and perform 'a man's job.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use convalescent and bedridden-capable work assignments to aid recovery and maintain pay
rubrics_metrics.description: "We put black oilcloth covers or aprons over the beds and set the men to work screwing nuts on small bolts... The men in the hospital could do it just as well as the men in the shop and they were able to receive their regular wages."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where feasible, arrange light, hand-performed tasks (e.g., screwing nuts) for convalescent or bedridden-yet-capable workers; participation aids recovery and keeps earnings steady.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide appropriate training durations and pathways to skilled trades
rubrics_metrics.description: "The length of time required to become proficient in the various occupations is about as follows: 43%... not over one day; 36%... one day to one week; 6%... one to two weeks; 14%... one month to one year; 1%... one to six years."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most jobs require minimal training; provide clear training time expectations and pathways (e.g., from production to tool-making or die sinking) for the few long-skill roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigid but impartial discipline with limited discharge authority and recourse
rubrics_metrics.description: "The discipline throughout the plant is rigid... The injustice of arbitrary discharge is avoided by confining the right of discharge to the employment manager, and he rarely exercises it... The workman has a full chance to tell his story if he has been unjustly treated--he has full recourse."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce strict attendance and job rules, investigate absences, and keep discharge power centralized to reduce arbitrary dismissals. Track reasons for separations and allow appeals or explanations to ensure fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect minimal hiring data and use a 'Better Advantage Notice' to locate prior trades
rubrics_metrics.description: "In hiring a man the only data taken concerns his name, his address, his age, whether he is married or single, the number of his dependents... whether he has ever worked for the Ford Motor Company, and the condition of his sight and his hearing... we have the 'Better Advantage Notice' by which a man who has had a trade before he came to us files a notice..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit intrusive questioning on hiring; record essential demographic and fitness-for-work information. Use voluntary notices to find prior trades when specialists are needed rather than screening by past history at hiring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a clean, well-lighted, and well-ventilated factory environment
rubrics_metrics.description: "One point that is absolutely essential to high capacity, as well as to humane production, is a clean, well-lighted and well-ventilated factory."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize floor-space usage (measure exact room needed per job), but ensure maximum safeguards and ventilation. Maintain cleanliness (dedicated cleaning staff) and daylight where possible; 'one cannot have morale without cleanliness.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider machines improper unless they are absolutely safe; investigate every accident
rubrics_metrics.description: "We do not consider any machine--no matter how efficiently it may turn out its work--as a proper machine unless it is absolutely safe... Every accident, no matter how trivial, is traced back by a skilled man... and a study is made of the machine to make that same accident in the future impossible."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have dedicated accident-investigation personnel. Trace each accident to root causes and redesign or safeguard machinery to prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal causes of accidents to address (12-point checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of principal causes: (1) Defective structures; (2) defective machines; (3) insufficient room; (4) absence of safeguards; (5) unclean conditions; (6) bad lights; (7) bad air; (8) unsuitable clothing; (9) carelessness; (10) ignorance; (11) mental condition; (12) lack of cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the easily-disposed causes through construction, wages, and organization; guard against unsuitable clothing, carelessness, and ignorance via safeguards, training, and design. Ensure mental fitness by reasonable hours/wages and foster cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard moving parts (belts) and prefer individual motors in new construction
rubrics_metrics.description: "In all of our new construction, each machine has its individual electric motor, but in the older construction we had to use belts. Every belt is guarded."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, equip machines with individual motors to eliminate belt hazards; where belts remain, provide guards. Design new buildings and machinery layouts to minimize belt-related risks and make systems 'fool-proof.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid petty personal management and minimize opportunities for personality conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is not much personal contact--the men do their work and go home--a factory is not a drawing room. But we try to have justice and... we try to prevent opportunity for petty personalities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize many departments so each person can find a suitable place; devise punishments that do not harm workers' families and avoid arbitrary, personal reprisals. Structure management to reduce favoritism and interpersonal causes of conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical practice: limit employment of married women when husbands are employed
rubrics_metrics.description: "Eighty-two women were discharged because their husbands were working--we do not employ married women whose husbands have jobs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was a stated employment policy in the text's historical context; include as a documented practice rather than a recommended modern standard. (Recorded for historical completeness.)
